issues.description: The problem description text requires a milk method with a double parameter (messageOnMilk(double milkVolume)), but the UML, the example usage in the template Main, and the solution implementation define messageOnMilk() with no parameters. This mismatch will confuse students about which signature to implement and will cause incompatibility with the provided solution/tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification consistent: either change the problem text to require messageOnMilk() with no parameters (to match the UML, template usage, and solution), or update the UML, template Main, and solution to use messageOnMilk(double milkVolume). Preferably adjust the problem statement wording to describe the no-argument messageOnMilk() signature (and the expected return string) to avoid breaking the intended interfaces and tests.

issues.description: The problem statement asks for a method messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) that includes a milk volume in its signature and return value, but both the provided template usage and the solution implement messageOnMilk() with no parameters. This creates a mismatch in the same conceptual entity (the milk action/message) across artifacts and will confuse students about the required method signature and expected output format.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the problem statement and code. Either (A) update the problem statement to require messageOnMilk() with no parameters and the return format without volume (e.g. "[Animal Type] [name] is milked"), matching the template and solution; or (B) change the interface and all implementations/call sites to use messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) and update calls (e.g. m.messageOnMilk(1.0)) and the expected return format to include the volume. Option A is the least disruptive given the current template and solution.
